Predict with an RLT forest

Source: R/predict.r
predict.RLT.Rd

Predict the outcome (regression, classification or survival) using a fitted RLT object

Usage

# S3 method for class 'RLT'
predict(
  object,
  testx = NULL,
  var.est = FALSE,
  var.mode = NULL,
  keep.all = FALSE,
  ncores = 1,
  verbose = 0,
  band.grid.size = 0,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted RLT object

testx

New observations with the training feature structure. If omitted, returns the stored OOB object$Prediction directly. For supplied data, labels are matched using the saved training dictionaries; numerical values for encoded features mean integer training codes. Legacy fits require their original dictionaries or refitting before accepting labels.

var.est

Whether to estimate prediction uncertainty. Fit with an active var.mode, or satisfy the requirements for an explicit prediction-time mode described below. Regression returns prediction variance; classification returns variance for each class probability. Survival returns cumulative-hazard covariance over the evaluation times.

var.mode

Variance estimation mode for prediction. Can be "none", "matched", "IJ", or "jack". If NULL (default), uses the mode from the fitted object. Only used when var.est = TRUE. "matched" requires the forest to be fitted with var.mode = "matched". "IJ" and "jack" require the forest to have been fitted with resample tracking (automatically enabled when using IJ or jack variance).

keep.all

whether to keep the prediction from all trees. Warning: this can occupy a large storage space, especially in survival model

ncores

number of cores

verbose

print additional information

band.grid.size

A nonnegative integer specifying the requested maximum number of evaluation time points. Default is 0, which uses all unique failure time points. If a positive integer is provided, a subset of time points will be selected using quantiles from the fifth percentile through the last time point. Quantile selection may return fewer distinct points. A request of 1 selects the fifth-percentile point.

...

...

Value

With testx = NULL, returns object$Prediction directly, without a prediction list. Otherwise returns an RLT prediction list.

For regression and classification:

Prediction

Regression: an \(N \times 1\) numeric matrix. Classification: a factor of predicted labels using the training response levels. Here N = nrow(testx).

Prob

Classification only: an \(N \times K\) matrix of class probabilities, with columns in the order of the fitted object's ylabels, where K is the number of classes.

Variance

When variance estimation is requested, regression prediction variances or an \(N \times K\) matrix of class-probability variances. Negative variance estimates are returned as NA.

For Survival Forests

Hazard, CHF and Survival each have one row per test observation and one column per evaluation time. There is no Prediction component in this list.

Hazard

predicted pointwise hazard increments at the selected times

CHF

predicted cumulative hazard, accumulated on the complete training grid before selecting evaluation times. On a reduced grid, accumulating only Hazard does not in general reproduce CHF.

Survival

ordinary forests return exp(-CHF). Linear combination forests return the mean of the tree product-limit survival curves. The get.surv.band() interface uses exp(-CHF) as its reference curve.

AllHazard

if keep.all = TRUE, the pointwise hazard increments for each tree, selected time, and observation, in that array order

Cov

when variance estimation is requested, an array with one \(T\times T\) cumulative-hazard covariance matrix per test subject, where T = length(timepoints). Its dimensions are time, time, and test observation, in that order.

timepoints

ordered evaluation times selected from the training failure grid

Examples

# \donttest{
  set.seed(42)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(300 * 5), ncol = 5)
  y <- rowSums(x[, 1:2]) + rnorm(300)
  fit <- RLT(x, y, ntrees = 100)
  pred <- predict(fit, testx = x[1:5, ])
  print(pred$Prediction)
#>             [,1]
#> [1,]  1.22292224
#> [2,]  0.28236394
#> [3,] -0.09172784
#> [4,]  1.41876752
#> [5,] -0.27677253
# }
